(CNN) -- Prince Harry paraded alongside his fellow British servicemen in Scotland Wednesday, as he attended a memorial to service members who have died in Afghanistan. Prince Harry takes part in a memorial parade and service for troops killed during his tour of Afghanistan. Harry, 23, serves in the British Army and spent 10 weeks in Afghanistan earlier this year. He was withdrawn unexpectedly in March after news leaked out about his low-key deployment. The prince appeared in uniform alongside around 200 other sailors, soldiers, marines and airmen at the parade, which took place on Edinburgh's famous Royal Mile. They made their way to St. Giles' Cathedral for a private memorial and thanksgiving service for the fallen service members. Also attending the service was British Defense Secretary Des Browne, families of the fallen troops, and recovering wounded military personnel. Harry holds the rank of cornet, equivalent to a second lieutenant. He was deployed to Afghanistan's Helmand province where he served as a forward air controller. His duties included calling in airstrikes and air support when necessary, guaranteeing the accuracy of bombing on the ground and guarding against incidents of friendly fire. The parade and memorial service took place on the same day Britain's Ministry of Defense announced the deaths of four British soldiers in Afghanistan, and two days after Browne announced Britain will increase its presence in Afghanistan from 7,800 troops to 8,030 by next spring.  Watch Prince Harry at the memorial » . Prince Harry is the younger son of Prince Charles, the heir to the British throne, and the late Princess Diana, who died in a Paris car crash in 1997. Last year, the military ruled he could not be sent to Iraq because publicity about the deployment could put him and his unit at risk. Shortly after the news of the prince's deployment broke, several Islamist Web sites posted messages alerting their "brethren" in Afghanistan to be on the lookout for the royal soldier. Several members of the British royal family saw combat in the past century. Prince Harry's grandfather, Prince Phillip, served aboard warships in World War II; his great-grandfather -- the future King George VI -- took part in the World War I naval battle of Jutland; and Prince Andrew, Prince Harry's uncle, flew Royal Navy helicopters during Britain's 1982 war with Argentina over the Falkland Islands. Prince Harry's brother, Prince William, is also an army officer. But as second in line for the throne, he is specifically barred from combat.

# Prince Harry Joins Fellow Servicemen in Solemn Afghanistan Memorial

(CNN) -- Prince Harry marched alongside his fellow British servicemen through Scotland on Wednesday, joining a solemn commemoration for those who have lost their lives in Afghanistan. The 23-year-old prince, who currently serves in the British Army, participated in a memorial parade and service honoring troops killed during the course of his own deployment earlier this year.

Harry had spent 10 weeks stationed in Afghanistan before being unexpectedly withdrawn in March, after his previously undisclosed deployment was revealed in the press. On Wednesday, he appeared in full military uniform alongside approximately 200 fellow sailors, soldiers, marines, and airmen, processing along Edinburgh's historic Royal Mile before arriving at St. Giles' Cathedral for a private memorial and thanksgiving service dedicated to the fallen.

Among those in attendance were British Defense Secretary Des Browne, grieving families of the deceased, and wounded military personnel still in recovery.

Holding the rank of cornet—equivalent to a second lieutenant—Harry had served in Afghanistan's Helmand province as a forward air controller. His responsibilities in that role included coordinating airstrikes and air support, ensuring the precision of ground-targeted bombing operations, and helping to prevent incidents of friendly fire.

The memorial coincided with a somber announcement from Britain's Ministry of Defense confirming the deaths of four additional British soldiers in Afghanistan. It also came just two days after Secretary Browne revealed plans to expand Britain's military presence in the country, increasing troop numbers from 7,800 to 8,030 by the following spring.

**Watch Prince Harry at the memorial »**

Prince Harry is the younger son of Prince Charles, heir to the British throne, and the late Princess Diana, who tragically died in a car accident in Paris in 1997. The previous year, military officials had determined that Harry could not be deployed to Iraq, citing concerns that public awareness of his presence there might endanger both him and his unit. Indeed, shortly after news of his eventual Afghanistan deployment emerged, several Islamist websites published messages urging their "brethren" in the region to watch for the royal soldier.

Military service runs deep within the royal family's recent history. Prince Harry's grandfather, Prince Philip, served aboard warships during World War II, while his great-grandfather—the future King George VI—fought in the historic World War I naval Battle of Jutland. Prince Andrew, Harry's uncle, piloted Royal Navy helicopters during the 1982 Falklands War with Argentina.

Prince Harry's older brother, Prince William, also holds a commission as an army officer. However, as second in line to the throne, William remains explicitly prohibited from serving in combat roles.
